title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Templates (Narrative Guidance)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This narrative playbook supplements Redwood Inference's operational standards by walking readers through typical incident lifecycles with concrete examples. It covers incident classification and SLAs, the notification and escalation model, runbook structure and a worked example, postmortem expectations, rotation and handoff etiquette, quarterly game-days, and status/customer communications templates. The goal is to make on-call execution predictable and to reduce time-to-mitigation through clear roles, checklists, and reusable text templates.

1. Incident classification and SLA expectations:
- Sev 1 (P0): total or near-total service outage or data-loss event. Acknowledge within 5 minutes. IC assembled within 15 minutes. First public status update within 30 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1): significant functional degradation (high latency, partial regional outage, broad customer impact). Acknowledge within 15 minutes. Mitigation plan within 60 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P2): limited impact, single region or single feature. Acknowledge within 4 hours; work in normal hours unless escalated.
- Sev 4 (P3): informational or maintenance-related. Tracked in tickets, no pager.

2. Notification & escalation flow (operational example):
- Alert fires in Prometheus/CloudWatch -> Alertmanager -> webhook -> PagerDuty service for the affected team.
- PagerDuty routing: primary on-call -> (after escalation_timeout) secondary -> (after second timeout) team lead and SRE manager.
- For P0s, SMS is enabled and Slack #oncall-alerts is notified automatically. Ensure phone numbers in PagerDuty are current and verified.

3. Roles & responsibilities (how a typical P0 unfolds):
- Primary: acknowledges alert, posts initial findings to incident doc, owns immediate mitigation steps from the runbook.
- Secondary: assists with triage, validates mitigations and performs cross-checks (e.g., verifies GPU pool health).
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates cross-team work, sets meeting cadence, assigns action items. Typically the SRE lead or a senior engineer.
- Communications Lead: drafts customer-facing and internal status updates; publishes to status.redwood.ai following approval by Support Lead.
- Postmortem Author: compiles timeline and analysis after service is restored.

4. Runbook structure (required fields):
- Title (short), Service name, Owner team, PagerDuty service ID, Runbook owner contact, Last updated date, SLOs affected, Symptoms, Immediate checks (numbered), Quick mitigations (ordered), Full remediation (step-by-step), Verification steps, Post-incident tasks, Changelog.

5. Runbook worked example (hosted-api high-latency):
- Symptom observed: p95 > 1.2s across regions for >10 minutes, streaming reconnects rising.
- Immediate checks (first 10 minutes):
  1) Open Grafana runtime-overview dashboard and validate p50/p95/p99.
  2) Query Prometheus: hd_api_request_latency_p95{env="prod"}.
  3) Check model-serving node GPU utilization and queue depth.
  4) Inspect last deploys (CI tags) and config rollout timestamps.
- Quick mitigations (fast path):
  1) Apply routing policy to fallback model variant (CLI: rwdctl traffic-route set --service hosted-api --fallback-variant small-enc-quant).
  2) Temporarily widen batching window or reduce batch size depending on latency profile (console or API).
  3) If pods are unhealthy, restart runtime-worker pods: kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker.
- Verification: p95 back under 1.2s for 15 continuous minutes, error rate steady and streaming reconnects normalized.

6. Postmortem process & expectations:
- Immediately after mitigation, the Primary or IC creates an incident document with title and incident id.
- Postmortem draft due within 72 hours of incident end. Should include: timeline (UTC), impact summary (customers, endpoints, duration), root cause statement, contributing factors, detection & response analysis, action items with owners and due dates, and links to logs and dashboards.
- Review meeting scheduled within 7 days; attendees include owners and cross-team stakeholders. Critical action items tagged in Jira with priority P1 and due within 30 days.

7. On-call rotations & handoffs (practical rules):
- Standard cadence: 1-week primary on-call; teams may adopt 1-week or 2-week secondary schedules. Avoid >2 consecutive weeks for the same engineer.
- Handoff checklist (required before ending shift):
  - Post a handoff message to #oncall-handoffs with active incidents and mitigation status.
  - Share links to runbooks and recent deploys.
  - Note any silenced alerts or maintenance windows.
  - Confirm contactability during the next 24 hours if you are out of office.

8. Game days (quarterly simulation checklist):
- Objectives: validate runbooks, measure detection-to-ack and ack-to-mitigation times, test cross-team escalation, and confirm status page workflow.
- Logistics: schedule two weeks in advance, prepare synthetic traffic and a rollback plan, define scoring rubrics for observers.
- After action: publish a short game-day report within 48 hours and convert findings to tracked Jira issues.

9. Status page & customer communications (templates and cadence):
- Initial message (first public update for P0):
  "We are investigating elevated errors affecting text-generation for some customers. Our engineers are actively investigating and we will post updates every 30 minutes. Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-XXX."
- Mitigation update (when mitigation underway):
  "Mitigation in progress: traffic is being routed to a fallback model variant and streaming sessions are stabilizing. We expect partial recovery in 30-60 minutes."
- Resolution & RCA summary (customer-facing):
  "Service restored at 2026-02-15T15:12:00Z. Root cause: a configuration rollout caused batching misrouting, increasing queue depth on runtime nodes. We rolled back the change and added a pre-deploy validation. Impact: 12:11-15:12 UTC, ~6% of requests returned 5xx. No customer data was lost."
- Internal status entry: include incident id, severity, regions affected, mitigation steps, verification metrics, links to postmortem and runbooks, and list of open action items.

10. Communication best practices:
- Keep public updates concise and non-technical; provide a technical appendix if needed.
- Maintain a cadence: initial (within SLA window), then every 30-60 minutes for ongoing incidents.
- Confirm message with Support Lead before publishing customer-facing RCA.

11. Maintenance and lifecycle for runbooks & incident docs:
- Update runbooks after any incident where the runbook was used. Record the change in the changelog section.
- Annual owner confirmation required for each runbook documented (last_updated field and review note).
- Archive runbooks that no longer apply and retain historical versions for audits.

Appendix: useful commands & links (examples)
- Prometheus quick query: curl -g 'https://prom.example.com/api/v1/query?query=hd_api_request_latency_p95{env="prod"}'
- Restart runtime worker: kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker
- Route traffic to fallback: rwdctl traffic-route set --service hosted-api --fallback-region eu-west-1
- PagerDuty: Services -> Hosted API -> escalation policies and schedule verification
